title: Tor amplitude and $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $X$ a scheme. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], write $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ for its internal module objects [det-def-sfb-module-objects-sheaves], identified with the category $\Mod(\Lambda_X)$ of sectionwise module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], and use its unbounded derived category and cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor below is the relative derived tensor over $\Lambda_X$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]; a module $N$ in such an expression is placed in degree zero.

1. $\Cons(X,\Lambda)\subset\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of
   constructible $\Lambda_X$-modules (strata on which the module has a finite constant local
   model, [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]). Here the constructibility convention is that of the source's parent definition: for qcqs $X$ use a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] by constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset] locally closed subschemes, and for arbitrary $X$ impose this condition locally on affine opens.
2. $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)\subset D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of complexes
   $K$ with $H^q(K)=0$ for all but finitely many $q$ and every $H^q(K)$ in $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$.
3. For integers $a\le b$, $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ has *Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$*
   if $H^q(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ and every
   $\Lambda_X$-module $N$; it has *finite Tor amplitude* if this holds for some $a\le b$.
4. $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\subset\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of complexes of finite
   Tor amplitude.

**Well-definedness.** All four conditions are invariant under isomorphism in the respective
categories, so these are full replete subcategories. If $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ then
$K[1]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-1,b-1]$. If $K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ is a distinguished
triangle and $K',K''$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, so does $K$; and a direct summand of a
complex with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Hence the complexes of
finite Tor amplitude form a thick subcategory (a full replete triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-category] closed under direct summands) of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, and
$\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is the intersection of this thick subcategory with $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Use the four definitions in the statement. If $M\simeq M'$, restrict this isomorphism to every stratum and every member of its pro-étale cover; composing with each local-model isomorphism supplies exactly the same finitely presented scalar modules and the same stratification for $M'$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Thus constructibility is invariant under isomorphism, including its affine-local convention. The cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] carry an isomorphism $K\simeq L$ to isomorphisms $H^q(K)\simeq H^q(L)$; both vanishing and constructibility of these objects are unchanged. For each fixed module $N[0]$, the relative derived tensor bifunctor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] also carries $K\simeq L$ to an isomorphism after tensoring, so each specified Tor interval, and hence the existence of one, is unchanged. Taking all morphisms between objects satisfying each condition gives the full subcategories asserted; the preceding invariance makes them replete.

source.place: Well-definedness, invariance under isomorphism; proof paragraph 1

proof.text: The small pro-étale site is chosen small relative to the universe of the module sheaves, as allowed by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] (a universe convention, not a finiteness assumption on $X$ or $\Lambda$), and abelian sheafification $a$ exists. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] $a$ is strong monoidal, $a(F\otimes_pG)\cong a(F)\otimes a(G)$; hence if $a(f)$ is invertible, so is $a(f\otimes_pG)\cong a(f)\otimes a(G)$: local equivalences are monoidal. These are the hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], applied to the commutative monoid $\Lambda_X$. Its equivalence $E$ identifies internal $\Lambda_X$-modules with sectionwise modules over the reconstructed commutative section-ring sheaf, preserving underlying abelian sheaves, sections and restriction maps. It is additive and exact because biproducts, kernels and cokernels are characterized by universal properties, which an equivalence preserves. Abelian sheaves have coequalizers, and $\mathcal F\otimes-$, $-\otimes\mathcal F$ preserve colimits by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-closed], so the hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] hold. Its relative coequalizer represents maps $\phi$ out of $M\otimes N$ with $\phi(rm,n)=\phi(m,rn)$; requiring the induced map to be $\Lambda_X$-linear makes these exactly the sectionwise $\Lambda_X$-bilinear maps. By [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] the ordinary sheaf tensor $\otimes_{\Lambda_X}$ represents the same functor, so the unique isomorphism of representing objects identifies the two relative tensor products naturally, and the regular module identifies their units.

Applying $E$ degreewise preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. It preserves shifts and sends the cone matrix $\begin{pmatrix}d_L&f\\0&-d_K\end{pmatrix}$ to the cone matrix for $E(f)$, since it preserves finite biproducts and addition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence $E$ and its inverse induce exact equivalences of derived categories. Preservation of direct sums and the tensor comparison identify total tensor complexes and preserve K-flatness: tensoring with an acyclic complex is acyclic on one side exactly when it is on the other. The Layer B statement [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is precisely the relative tensor used above, so a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ is carried to one and $E(P\otimes_{\Lambda_X}N)\simeq E(P)\otimes_{\Lambda_X}E(N)$ computes the corresponding derived tensors.

source.place: blueprint proof paragraph 2, derived tensor comparison

proof.text: Apply the exactness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to the identity morphism of the ringed topos $(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda_X)$ with its identity ring map. The site presentation is chosen small relative to the universe of module sheaves, as allowed by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; this is only a universe convention. Thus for each degree-zero module $N$ the functor $T_N(K)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}N$ is exact. By [def-weil-triangulated-category], exactness supplies $T_N(K[1])\simeq T_N(K)[1]$. The shift convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $H^q(L[1])\simeq H^{q+1}(L)$, since the sign changes neither kernel nor image. Therefore an interval $[a,b]$ shifts to $[a-1,b-1]$, and applying the same argument to $K[-1]$ gives $[a+1,b+1]$.

For a distinguished triangle $K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ and a module $N[0]$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] makes its image under $T_N$ a distinguished triangle. Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] in the abelian category of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves. For $q\notin[a,b]$ the exact segment $H^q(T_NK')\to H^q(T_NK)\to H^q(T_NK'')$ has both outside objects zero, so the middle object is zero. This proves the extension bound uniformly for every $N$.

Take a retract $E\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{r}E$ with $ri=1_E$. The tensor bifunctor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] and cohomology functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] carry this identity to $H^q(T_Nr)H^q(T_Ni)=1_{H^q(T_NE)}$. If $K$ has amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $q$ is outside that interval, this composite factors through $H^q(T_NK)=0$, so the identity of $H^q(T_NE)$ is zero. Hence this object is zero for every $N$. A direct summand of $K$ is such a retract through its inclusion and projection, so every direct summand of a complex of amplitude $[a,b]$ has amplitude in $[a,b]$; no splitting of idempotents is needed.

The zero object has amplitude $[0,0]$, because the exact tensor functors of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] are additive and preserve zero objects by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Enlarging an interval preserves its vanishings, so finitely many finite intervals have a common enlargement. Steps 4 and 5 give closure under shifts and extensions; in a triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ with $A,B$ of finite Tor amplitude, rotate it using [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $B\to C\to A[1]\to B[1]$ enlarge the intervals of $B$ and $A[1]$ to a common one, and apply the extension result to obtain finite Tor amplitude for $C$. The cone formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives finite biproducts: for representatives of $A[-1]$ and $B$, the cone of their zero map is $B\oplus A$ with the direct-sum differential. Thus the full replete subcategory is additive and closed under shifts and distinguished triangles; in [def-weil-triangulated-category], TR1 and TR2 restrict by cone and shift closure, TR3 restricts by fullness, and every further object in an ambient TR4 diagram is a cone of a morphism between objects already in the subcategory, so TR4 restricts as well. Step 6 gives closure under all existing direct summands, so it is thick. By clause 4 of the statement, its intersection with $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is exactly $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

split_report.summary: Split the imported definition into seven proof steps. The five blueprint well-definedness paragraphs are realized by an explicit internal-module/tensor comparison, the resulting derived equivalence and shifts, extension, retract, and thick-subcategory arguments. No new nodes were created; all non-elementary inputs are existing DAG statements, with off-unit generic tensor tools retained in tool_uses. The statement and hypotheses were checked against the main-20261015 blueprint and no correction was needed. Maintainer reading (FIX): restored the explicit hypothesis check of the internal/sectionwise module equivalence in step 2, the explicit summand-as-retract and TR3/TR4 restriction arguments in steps 6-7, and the {node, why} form of split_report.tool_uses.
split_report.blueprint: Paragraph 1 (isomorphism invariance), paragraph 2 (internal-module comparison, derived tensor comparison, shifts), paragraph 3 (extensions), paragraph 4 (summands), and paragraph 5 (thick closure and intersection).

tool_uses.why: Only the generic exactness of relative derived tensor on a commutative ringed site is used (steps 4, 5, 7), specialized to the identity ringed pro-etale topos. The unit defines derived tensor but has no node asserting its triangulated exactness.

The generic bilinear universal property identifies the internal relative coequalizer with the sectionwise sheaf tensor (step 2); it is used only for the coefficient-category comparison before applying the exact-tensor tool.

There are no new nodes. I read all 12 proof dependencies and the stmt deps in full. Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 are correct. Step 4 applies the exactness clause of the mate lemma to the identity ringed topos and uses H^q(L[1])=H^{q+1}(L); with K=Lambda_X[0], amplitude [0,0] becomes [-1,-1] after the shift. I made three repairs. (1) Step 2 said the hypotheses of def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence followed from colimit preservation, which is not one of them. It now checks them: site size by the universe convention of def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, and monoidal local equivalences from strong monoidality of sheafification. Colimit preservation now serves def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor. (2) Step 7 said 'TR1--TR4 restrict' without the argument (E5); it now gives TR1/TR2 by cone and shift closure, TR3 by fullness, TR4 because every extra object is a cone of a map inside the subcategory, and writes the biproduct as the cone of a zero map. Step 6 now says a direct summand is a retract, so no idempotent splitting is needed. (3) split_report.tool_uses had been reduced to bare ids; it is back in {node, why} form. I accept both tool uses, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact (generic exactness of derived tensor only) and lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal. No cycle, no SGA, statement unchanged.
